property_summary: When calling fallback with msg.value==10 ether, the update to pastBlockTime must increase or stay equal (non-decreasing) relative to the previous value.
After a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, the new pastBlockTime is always greater than the old pastBlockTime.
After any fallback call that reverts due to the timestamp requirement (msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp <= pastBlockTime), the value of pastBlockTime must not change.
After any successful fallback call (msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp not blocked), pastBlockTime must be set to the current block.timestamp, not exceed it.

After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, pastBlockTime must be greater than the previous value only when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime; with the mutant's '<', it incorrectly updates when block.timestamp < pastBlockTime.
After any call, pastBlockTime must be greater than the previous pastBlockTime.
After a fallback call with msg.value != 10 ether, the pastBlockTime must not be updated.
For any valid call to fallback, the contract never reverts due to the timestamp check when the caller sends exactly 10 ether.
The block timestamp must never be equal to pastBlockTime after a successful fallback call that sends 10 ether.

After any sequence of fallback calls sending 10 ether, the contract balance is always at least as large as the number of successful calls times 10 ether, but the mutant can lose balance due to a timestamp equality reversion.
When a fallback call sends exactly 10 ether and the timestamp equals pastBlockTime, the call reverts in the reference but succeeds in the mutant, leading to a balance difference.
When msg.value is 10 ether and block.number is not a multiple of 15, the contract's balance must remain unchanged after the fallback call.
After a successful fallback call with msg.value = 10 ether, the block.timestamp must always be strictly greater than the previous pastBlockTime.
After any fallback call with msg.value = 10 ether, the next fallback call with msg.value = 10 ether at a later timestamp must succeed (not revert).
After each fallback call with msg.value = 10 ether, pastBlockTime is strictly increasing.
After a fallback call with exactly 10 ether, if block.number is not a multiple of 15 and the call does not revert, then the contract's balance decreases by exactly 10 ether.
After a non-reverting call to the fallback function, the contract's balance remains zero if the call succeeded.
After a call to the fallback with value exactly 1 ether, the contract's balance never increases by more than 1 ether unless the block number is a multiple of 15.
After a non-reverting call to the fallback function, pastBlockTime is always equal to block.timestamp if the call succeeds.
After a non-reverting call to the fallback function with msg.value == 10 ether, the contract's pastBlockTime is always updated to the current block timestamp.

After a successful fallback call with msg.value equal to 10 ether, the contract's balance can only decrease or stay the same, never increase, because the only payable call that can increase balance requires exactly 10 ether.
If block.number is divisible by 15, the contract's balance does not change after a payable fallback call with exactly 10 ether.
After a payable fallback call with exactly 10 ether, if block number is divisible by 15, the contract's balance stays the same as before the call.
After a fallback call with exactly 10 ether, if block.number is not divisible by 15, the contract's balance increases by exactly 10 ether.
After a successful payable fallback with exactly 10 ether, the sender's balance increases by exactly 10 ether when block.number is divisible by 15.
After a payable fallback call with exactly 10 ether, the contract's balance always increases by exactly 10 ether when block.number is not divisible by 15.
The contract should only transfer balance when block.number % 15 == 0
After any sequence of calls, if the contract's balance is 0, then the last call did not revert when the condition block.number % 15 == 0 is true.
After the fallback function is called with 10 ether, the contract's balance is zero exactly when block.number % 15 == 0.
After calling fallback with 10 ether, the contract's balance decreases by at most 0 ether (i.e., balance increases or stays same) only when block.number % 15 != 0.
After calling fallback with 10 ether, the contract's balance before the call is always less than or equal to the balance after the call when block.number % 15 == 0
The contract always transfers the full balance when triggered at a block number divisible by 15.
When triggered, the contract always sends the full balance; any division would reduce it.
After a fallback call with exactly 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, when the block number is divisible by 15, the contract's balance is reduced by exactly the amount sent to the caller.
After a successful fallback call that triggers the payout (block.number % 15 == 0), the contract balance decreases by exactly the full balance sent (not half).
When a fallback call triggers a payout, the contract sends its entire balance to the caller.
